title: Official talk
job: Announcements, offices and counters: the formal register you hear
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: THE FORMAL REGISTER ARRIVES HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE IN THIS COURSE. Every sentence in this module is chipped formal, and HALF OF WHAT IT TEACHES IS RECEPTION: these are lines you read on a board or hear across a counter. You answer them in the neutral register you have spoken since L1 — S09 and S10 are chipped neutral for exactly that reason. Speak this way to a friend and you have learned the wrong thing.

THE PASSIVE OPENS IN THREE CELLS AND NO MORE: kriyate 'is done', dīyate 'is given', ucyate 'is called'. All three are third singular, and there is no fourth. No other verb takes a passive here, no other person or number is written, and the passive participle stays shut.

EACH PASSIVE CELL IS A SHAPE OF A VERB YOU ALREADY HAVE. kriyate belongs to L1-M4's karoti, dīyate to L1-M3's dadātu, and ucyate to L3-M5's uktavān — which is the vac- word L3-M5 gave a row of its own precisely because it is not a shape of L2-M7's vadati.

WHAT THE ACTIVE VERB REACHED FOR BECOMES THE SUBJECT. kāryam karoti is 'does the work', with kāryam as the object; kāryam kriyate is 'the work is done', with the same word now the naming shape and the whole sentence built around it.

AN OFFICIAL SANSKRIT SENTENCE NAMES NO AGENT AT ALL, and that is why the register uses the passive. English officialese still says 'by the office', so a learner reaches for an instrumental — and L4-M1's mayā and bhavatā, which are right for a gerundive, are wrong here and appear nowhere in this module.

niṣiddhaḥ IS 'FORBIDDEN', AND IT IS A SIGN-WORD RATHER THAN A PATTERN. It has the shape of a past participle, and this course does not build that shape productively — jātam (L2-M8) was the first frozen one and niṣiddhaḥ is the second and the last. It agrees with what it forbids: praveśaḥ niṣiddhaḥ.

THE SIGN'S REAL PROHIBITION IS L4-M1's GERUNDIVE NEGATED: atra na gantavyam, 'one must not go in here', and atra kāryam na kartavyam. Nobody is named, nothing is commanded at anybody, and that impersonality is the whole formal effect.

kāryālayasamayaḥ IS THREE MEMBERS IN ONE WORD — kārya, ālaya, samaya — with the joins written in full, because internal sandhi inside a single token always is. It is ONE word row: tapping it gives you the compound, not kāryālayaḥ and not samayaḥ, and all three are taught separately.

A REAL BOARD RUNS THE WORDS TOGETHER AND THIS COURSE STILL DOES NOT. Printed and recited Sanskrit carries its external sandhi, so a sign really is set as one flowing line. The display here stays in pada form, word by word and tappable, and the joined reading is given in the usage line instead. That was decided for the whole course and this is the module it was decided for.

WHAT THE FORMAL REGISTER DOES NOT BRING WITH IT. No prohibition with mā and an imperative — a sign says niṣiddhaḥ or na kartavyam. No vocative, which a counter wants more than anything else here. No passive of any other verb and none in any other person. No second-person ending anywhere, so a clerk is still bhavān or bhavatī with a third-person verb. And the formal chip belongs to this module alone.

words.note: L1-M7's 'here'. On a sign it means 'at this door' and nothing more.
'Entry', masculine. It is the subject of the commonest sign in the language, and niṣiddhaḥ agrees with it.
'Forbidden'. A frozen sign-word, not a pattern to build on: this course writes only two words of this shape, L2-M8's jātam and this one.

sentences.trap: There is no verb at all and none is missing. Two nouns in the naming shape are a complete Sanskrit sentence, and a sign is where that is most obvious.

variations.cue: Entry is not forbidden here.
variations.changed: L1-M2's na negates the sign; niṣiddhaḥ does not change shape, because na stands in front of what it denies

variations.cue: Entry to the office is forbidden.
variations.changed: the place moves from a bare 'here' to L3-M8's office in its 'in' shape — a sign names its own door

variations.cue: One must not go in here.
variations.changed: the same prohibition written as L4-M1's gerundive instead of as a participle; this is what a notice usually says

sentences.usage: Printed on a board the two words run together as praveśo niṣiddhaḥ, because recited and printed Sanskrit carries its sandhi. This course writes them apart so each stays tappable.
sentences.mnemonic: Entry: forbidden. Two words, no verb.

sentences.cue: The notice reads: one must not go in here.

words.note: L1-M7's 'here', inside the quoted line rather than outside it.
L1-M2's 'not', in front of the gerundive it denies.
L4-M1's gerundive. Negated it is a prohibition, and it names nobody — which is the whole formal effect.
L3-M5's quotative, standing behind the words it closes. It never comes first and there is no word for 'that'.
'A notice', feminine. It heads what is posted: a quoted line, then iti, then sūcanā, exactly as L3-M5 taught the quotative.

variations.display: atra kāryam na kartavyam iti sūcanā.
variations.script: अत्र कार्यम् न कर्तव्यम् इति सूचना।
variations.cue: The notice reads: work must not be done here.
variations.changed: the prohibition changes verb, and kartavyam is the second of L4-M1's three gerundive cells

variations.cue: The notice reads: entry is forbidden here.
variations.changed: the quoted line becomes the participle sign instead of the gerundive — two ways to write one board

variations.cue: Must one not go in here?
variations.changed: L1-M2's kim makes a question of the prohibition, which is what a visitor asks at a counter

mistake.why: iti has been dropped. Without it the quoted line and the word for the notice simply sit side by side, and nothing marks where the posted words end.

sentences.usage: How a posted line is reported: the words as posted, then iti, then what they are.

sentences.cue: Work is done at the office every day.

words.note: L3-M8's office in its 'in' shape, which L1-M7 made the place case.
L1-M4's 'daily'.

words.cue: work · the thing to be done
words.note: L3-M2's work. In an active sentence it would be what the verb reaches for; here it is the subject.
The passive of L1-M4's karoti, third singular. What karoti would have reached for becomes the subject, and nobody is named as doing it.

sentences.trap: Nobody is named as doing the work, and adding a 'by' would be the English sentence rather than the Sanskrit one. The agent's absence is the register.

variations.cue: No work is done at the office today.
variations.changed: the passive is negated and the day word changes; the missing agent stays missing, as it must

variations.cue: He does work at the office every day.
variations.changed: the active of the same verb, which needs somebody to do it — the third singular now points at a person

variations.cue: A certificate is issued at the office every day.
variations.changed: the second passive cell in the same frame, with the thing issued as the subject

sentences.usage: The line an office puts on its own board about itself.

sentences.cue: The certificate is issued at the office.

words.note: L3-M8's office in its 'in' shape.
L3-M8's certificate, a compound of two members. Here it is the subject of a passive.
The passive of L1-M3's dadātu, third singular. The thing given is the subject; the counter that gives it goes unmentioned.

variations.cue: The certificate is not issued at the office.
variations.changed: the passive is negated, which on a counter board means 'apply elsewhere'

variations.cue: The form is issued at the office.
variations.changed: the subject becomes L3-M8's plainer word, and the verb does not move, because a passive agrees with its subject's number and not with its meaning

variations.cue: Is the certificate issued here?
variations.changed: L1-M2's kim turns the board into the question a visitor asks in front of it

sentences.usage: Read off a counter; you answer it in your own everyday register, not in this one.

words.note: L1-M1's neuter 'this', agreeing with the neuter word it points at.
L3-M8's certificate. Inside the quote it is the name being given, not the thing being handed over.
L3-M5's quotative, closing the name. The naming formula is always X iti ucyate and never ucyate iti X.
The passive of L3-M5's uktavān, third singular. With iti in front it is 'is called X' — the naming formula of an official notice.

sentences.trap: The name comes first and iti closes it. Put ucyate before the name and you have said nothing that a Sanskrit ear can parse.

variations.cue: This is called a form.
variations.changed: the name changes and the frame does not — X iti ucyate takes any name at all

variations.cue: This is not called a certificate.
variations.changed: the naming is denied; na stands in front of the verb and never inside the quote

variations.cue: Is this called a certificate?
variations.changed: L1-M2's kim asks for the name, which is how you learn a word at a counter

sentences.usage: The formula a notice uses to define its own terms.

sentences.display: atra niyamaḥ asti, atra kāryam na kartavyam.
sentences.script: अत्र नियमः अस्ति, अत्र कार्यम् न कर्तव्यम्।
sentences.cue: There is a rule here: work must not be done here.
sentences.literal: here rule is, here work not to-be-done

words.note: L1-M7's 'here', opening both halves.
'A rule', masculine. It is what a sign is an instance of, and it sits in L1-M3's plain asti frame.
L1-M3's 'is · there is', which is all a rule needs to be announced.

words.cue: work · the thing to be done
words.note: L3-M2's work, the thing the gerundive is about.
L1-M2's 'not', in front of the gerundive.
L4-M1's gerundive of karoti. Negated it forbids, and it forbids nobody in particular.

variations.display: atra niyamaḥ asti, atra na gantavyam.
variations.script: अत्र नियमः अस्ति, अत्र न गन्तव्यम्।
variations.cue: There is a rule here: one must not go in here.
variations.changed: the prohibition changes to the going verb, which is the commonest gerundive on a board

variations.cue: There is no rule here.
variations.changed: the first half alone, negated — which is what a clerk says when a visitor asks

variations.cue: The rule is that work must be done here.
variations.changed: the halves are rebuilt round L3-M5's iti and the prohibition becomes an instruction

sentences.usage: Said by a clerk pointing at a board rather than by the board itself.

sentences.display: samayaḥ na asti, ataḥ adya patram na dīyate.
sentences.script: समयः न अस्ति, अतः अद्य पत्रम् न दीयते।
sentences.cue: There is no time, so the form is not issued today.
sentences.literal: time not is, therefore today form not is-given

words.note: 'Time', masculine — an appointed time rather than a clock reading. kāryālayasya samayaḥ is the office's time in two words; kāryālayasamayaḥ is the same in one.
L1-M2's 'not', in front of asti.
L1-M3's 'is · there is'.
L1-M9's consequence word. It may only head the consequence, never the cause.
L1-M4's 'today'.
L3-M8's form, the subject of the passive behind it.
L1-M2's 'not' again, this time denying the passive.
The passive of L1-M3's dadātu, third singular. The thing given is the subject; the counter that gives it goes unmentioned.

sentences.sound: sa-MA-yah na AS-ti, a-TAH A-dya PA-tram na DEE-ya-teh.

variations.display: samayaḥ asti, ataḥ adya patram dīyate.
variations.script: समयः अस्ति, अतः अद्य पत्रम् दीयते।
variations.cue: There is time, so the form is issued today.
variations.changed: both negations come out and the announcement turns from a closure into an opening

variations.display: samayaḥ na asti, ataḥ adya kāryam na kriyate.
variations.script: समयः न अस्ति, अतः अद्य कार्यम् न क्रियते।
variations.cue: There is no time, so no work is done today.
variations.changed: the consequence changes to the first passive cell; ataḥ still heads the consequence and never the cause

variations.display: yataḥ samayaḥ na asti, atra adya patram na dīyate.
variations.script: यतः समयः न अस्ति, अत्र अद्य पत्रम् न दीयते।
variations.cue: Because there is no time, the form is not issued here today.
variations.changed: L1-M9's yataḥ marks the cause instead, and one link is still marked once and not twice

mistake.display: samayaḥ na asti, ataḥ adya patram na dadātu.
mistake.why: dadātu is an imperative — 'please give'. An official line names nobody to ask, so the passive dīyate is the only shape that fits a counter closing for the day.

sentences.usage: The announcement over a counter at the end of a working day.

sentences.display: kāryālayasamayaḥ adhunā asti, ataḥ atra kāryam kriyate.
sentences.script: कार्यालयसमयः अधुना अस्ति, अतः अत्र कार्यम् क्रियते।
sentences.cue: It is office hours now, so work is being done here.
sentences.literal: office-time now is, therefore here work is-done

words.note: Three members in one word — kārya, ālaya, samaya — with the joins written in full. It is one row: tapping it gives the compound and not its parts.
L4-M6's 'now'.
L1-M3's 'is · there is'.
L1-M9's consequence word.
L1-M7's 'here'.

words.cue: work · the thing to be done
words.note: L3-M2's work, the subject of the passive.
The passive of L1-M4's karoti, third singular. What karoti would have reached for becomes the subject, and nobody is named as doing it.

sentences.trap: kāryālayasamayaḥ is one word and one tap. The office alone is kāryālayaḥ and the time alone is samayaḥ, and this course teaches all three separately because a compound hands nothing down to its members.
sentences.sound: KAAR-yaa-la-ya-sa-ma-yah a-dhu-NAA AS-ti, a-TAH A-tra KAAR-yam kri-YA-teh.

variations.cue: It is the office's time now.
variations.changed: the compound is taken apart into L3-M8's genitive plus the bare time word — the same meaning in two words instead of one

variations.display: kāryālayasamayaḥ adhunā na asti, ataḥ atra kāryam na kriyate.
variations.script: कार्यालयसमयः अधुना न अस्ति, अतः अत्र कार्यम् न क्रियते।
variations.cue: It is not office hours now, so no work is being done here.
variations.changed: both halves are negated and the announcement closes the counter rather than opening it

variations.display: kāryālayasamayaḥ adhunā asti, ataḥ atra pramāṇapatram dīyate.
variations.script: कार्यालयसमयः अधुना अस्ति, अतः अत्र प्रमाणपत्रम् दीयते।
variations.cue: It is office hours now, so certificates are issued here.
variations.changed: the consequence moves to the second passive cell, with the thing issued as its subject

sentences.usage: The line a counter puts up at opening time.

sentences.cue: I would like a certificate at the office.

words.note: L3-M8's office in its 'in' shape.
L1-M1's 'I'. A visitor speaks for themselves, which is exactly what the board never does.
L3-M8's certificate, here the thing wanted rather than the thing issued.
L1-M3's wanting verb in the first singular — the register you have spoken since L1 and the one you answer a board in.

sentences.trap: This sentence is chipped neutral on purpose. You read the formal line and you do not repeat it back; a visitor who says dīyate about their own wish has learned the register as a costume.

variations.cue: I would like a form at the office.
variations.changed: the thing wanted changes and nothing else does

variations.cue: The certificate is issued at the office.
variations.changed: the same business said from the other side of the counter, which is the formal line and is chipped formal

variations.cue: Please give me a certificate at the office.
variations.changed: L2-M1's kṛpayā with L1-M3's polite imperative — the everyday request, which names the person asked without a second-person ending

sentences.usage: What you actually say at the window. The board is formal; you are not.

sentences.display: atra praveśaḥ niṣiddhaḥ iti aham jānāmi.
sentences.script: अत्र प्रवेशः निषिद्धः इति अहम् जानामि।
sentences.cue: I know that entry is forbidden here.
sentences.literal: here entry forbidden thus I know

words.note: L1-M7's 'here', inside the quoted sign.
'Entry', masculine. It is the subject of the commonest sign in the language, and niṣiddhaḥ agrees with it.
'Forbidden'. A frozen sign-word, not a pattern to build on: this course writes only two words of this shape, L2-M8's jātam and this one.
L3-M5's quotative. It closes the posted words and there is no tense shift and no person shift across it.
L1-M1's 'I', outside the quote and in the everyday register.
L2-M8's knowing verb in the first singular. It is the frame a formal line is reported inside.

sentences.trap: The quote keeps the register it was posted in and the sentence round it keeps yours. Nothing about iti changes either half, which is what makes reception possible at all.
sentences.sound: A-tra pra-VEH-shah ni-SHID-dhah I-ti a-HAM jaa-NAA-mi.

variations.display: atra praveśaḥ niṣiddhaḥ iti aham na jānāmi.
variations.script: अत्र प्रवेशः निषिद्धः इति अहम् न जानामि।
variations.cue: I did not know that entry is forbidden here.
variations.changed: the reporting verb is negated; nothing inside the quote moves, because na belongs to the outer clause

variations.display: atra na gantavyam iti aham jānāmi.
variations.script: अत्र न गन्तव्यम् इति अहम् जानामि।
variations.cue: I know that one must not go in here.
variations.changed: the quoted sign becomes the gerundive version of itself and the frame is untouched

variations.display: atra praveśaḥ niṣiddhaḥ iti mama bhrātā uktavān.
variations.script: अत्र प्रवेशः निषिद्धः इति मम भ्राता उक्तवान्।
variations.cue: My brother said that entry is forbidden here.
variations.changed: the outer frame becomes L3-M5's verb of saying, so the sign is reported rather than known — and iti does not move for either

sentences.usage: How you tell somebody what a board said, in your own voice.
sentences.mnemonic: The sign is formal; the sentence around it is yours.

comprehensionPool.cue: The notice reads: entry is forbidden here.
No work is done at the office today.
Office hours are in the morning.

comprehensionPool.display: atra niyamaḥ asti, atra na gantavyam.
comprehensionPool.script: अत्र नियमः अस्ति, अत्र न गन्तव्यम्।
comprehensionPool.cue: There is a rule here: one must not go in.

comprehensionPool.display: kāryālaye pramāṇapatram na dīyate, ataḥ aham khinnaḥ.
comprehensionPool.script: कार्यालये प्रमाणपत्रम् न दीयते, अतः अहम् खिन्नः।
comprehensionPool.cue: The certificate is not issued at the office, so I am put out.

comprehensionPool.display: yadā kāryālayasamayaḥ asti tadā atra kāryam kriyate.
comprehensionPool.script: यदा कार्यालयसमयः अस्ति तदा अत्र कार्यम् क्रियते।
comprehensionPool.cue: When it is office hours, work is done here.
The notice reads: there is no time.

comprehensionPool.display: idam kāryam na kartavyam iti niyamaḥ.
comprehensionPool.script: इदम् कार्यम् न कर्तव्यम् इति नियमः।
comprehensionPool.cue: The rule is that this work must not be done.
It is not the office's time now.

comprehensionPool.display: prathamam śulkam dīyate, tataḥ pramāṇapatram dīyate.
comprehensionPool.script: प्रथमम् शुल्कम् दीयते, ततः प्रमाणपत्रम् दीयते।
comprehensionPool.cue: First the fee is paid, then the certificate is issued.
